title.narrative: Provision of Treatment and prevention of acute malnutrition among children, pregnant and lactating women at fixed Nutrition facilities and outreach in Baidoa Rural of Bay Region Southwest Somalia

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="font-family:"gtAccording to FSNAU’s 2022 Post Deyr assessment, global acute malnutrition (GAM) rates have remained critical, with Banadir, Baidoa, Afgooye, and Jowhar having the highest GAM burden. The 2023 HNO estimates that about 1.8 million children under five are likely to face acute malnutrition through mid-2023, with over 513,000 expected to be severely malnourished. The proposed project aims to address the urgent humanitarian needs arising from the sixth consecutive season of below-average rainfall in Somalia. The project will target approximately lt/spangtltb style="font-family:"gt24,030lt/bgtltspan style="font-family:"gt people in rural areas and lt/spangtltb style="font-family:"gt5000lt/bgtltspan style="font-family:"gt in Baidoa rural IDPs, in Baidoa rural Bay Region of Somalia, including children under five, who are among the most vulnerable. The project has four objectives, including providing equitable access to quality lifesaving curative nutrition services among boys and girls (06-59) months and PLW, preventing the loss of life of the most severely vulnerable people, strengthening lifesaving preventive nutrition services for vulnerable population groups, and preventing the loss of life of 6.7 million of the most vulnerable population in Somalia. To achieve these objectives, the project will systematically identify, refer, and treat acutely malnourished cases while focusing on improving nutritional status through the provision of supplementary nutrition products, appropriate infant and young child feeding practices, and micronutrient interventions. The project will engage community health workers (CHWs) to facilitate nutrition screening, health and nutrition education, and infant and young child feeding (IYCF) promotion. The CHWs will use a mother-led MUAC approach to identify and diagnose malnutrition by mothers, and mothers will be trained to screen for malnutrition, detect oedema, and self-refer their children to nutrition sites.lt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp style="mso-margin-top-alt:automso-margin-bottom-alt:auto line-height:normal" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family:"gtThe project will provide OTP/TSFP services to acutely malnourished under-five children (4191 boys and 5791 girls) and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs will be (4068) the total Number of children will be screening during the project period are (ltbgt29030lt/bgt and boys 7895 and Girls 9983) and integrate the management of acutely malnourished with ongoing routine health services at all levels. The project will provide routine immunization services to children and pregnant women in the project sites' catchment areas through both fixed and mobile OTP. Deworming, counselling and promotion on IYCF, and micronutrient supplementation for PLWs and children 6-59 months with Vitamin A supplements will also be provided. The project will work towards strengthening the local capacity for the integration of IMAM into the Primary Health Care system through functional MCH facilities. The project will also address survivors of gender-based violence (GBV) by coordinating with the Child Protection section to refer them from nutrition sites and catchment areas. The community approach will be overlaid with essential service provision of crucial nutrition basic services for prevention, promotion, and referral.lt/spangtlt/pgt
